title: Eliminating Disease-Carrying Pests and Restoring Enjoyment of the Great Outdoors

enrichment.summary: This executive order directs federal agencies to reduce populations of disease-carrying ticks and invasive mosquitoes, particularly in the District of Columbia, by using innovative, non-chemical methods and advanced technologies. It also promotes research for better diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases spread by these pests and ensures these efforts cause no harm to beneficial wildlife or the environment.
potential_concerns: The deployment of novel biotechnologies and sterile insect techniques may unintentionally disrupt local ecosystems, disproportionately affecting environmental justice communities who rely heavily on urban and suburban natural resources.

Urban and suburban residents might be concerned about the safety and transparency of releasing genetically modified or biologically engineered insects in their neighborhoods, raising public trust issues.

Agricultural workers and farmers could face increased pressures or operational challenges from enhanced pest control measures that affect surrounding wildlife and pest populations integral to their livelihoods.

Patients suffering from tick- and mosquito-borne diseases may experience delays or limitations in access to newly developed diagnostics and treatments if research priorities are not effectively coordinated or funded.
